features.name: green_red_ratio
features.description: Ratio of the green band (550.90 nm) to the red band (650.80 nm), capturing the relative reflectance peak often associated with specific biological or chemical compositions.
features.expected_model_benefit: Tree models can easily split on this ratio to isolate samples with distinct pigmentation or structural characteristics.

features.name: nir_red_difference
features.description: Difference between the near-infrared band (800.40 nm) and the red band (650.80 nm), serving as a proxy for structural scattering versus absorption.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a direct linear combination that trees can use to separate samples based on their red-edge transition magnitude.

features.name: blue_band_intensity_bucket
features.description: Categorize the blue band (451.10 nm) intensity into ordinal buckets (0=low, 1=medium, 2=high, 3=very high) based on typical spectral responses.
features.expected_model_benefit: Reduces noise and provides a robust ordinal feature that tree models can split on to group similar baseline reflectances.

features.name: is_high_green_peak
features.description: Boolean indicator for whether the green band (550.90 nm) exceeds a high intensity threshold of 1500.
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates a hard split for tree models to immediately partition highly reflective samples from darker ones.

features.name: red_edge_slope
features.description: Approximation of the red-edge slope by taking the difference between 700.70 nm and 650.80 nm.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the rate of change in reflectance, which is highly discriminative for biological materials in tree-based splits.

features.name: spectral_flatness_nir
features.description: Absolute difference between two NIR bands (800.40 nm and 899.90 nm) to measure the flatness of the spectrum in this region.
features.expected_model_benefit: Helps the model identify samples with flat vs. sloping NIR responses, providing a nonlinear interaction feature.

features.name: overall_brightness_proxy
features.description: Average intensity across three representative visible bands (blue, green, red) to estimate overall sample brightness.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a baseline intensity feature, allowing the tree to normalize or condition subsequent splits on overall brightness.

features.name: green_peak_prominence
features.description: Measures how much the green band (550.90 nm) stands out above the maximum of the blue (451.10 nm) and red (650.80 nm) bands.
features.expected_model_benefit: Directly quantifies the local maximum shape, which is a strong nonlinear feature for tree models to exploit.

features.name: uv_blue_dropoff
features.description: Difference between the shortest available wavelength (401.00 nm) and the blue band (451.10 nm).
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures absorption characteristics in the near-UV region, providing a distinct splitting criterion.

features.name: nir_noise_indicator
features.description: Assess whether the NIR region (800-1000nm) exhibits high noise or scattering by evaluating the variance and sudden spikes in the bands, returning a boolean-like indicator.
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows the tree to route noisy or highly scattered samples into separate leaf nodes, improving overall robustness.

features.name: red_absorption_depth
features.description: Calculates the depth of the red absorption feature by taking the positive difference between the green peak and the red trough.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a rectified, non-negative magnitude of absorption that trees can use to threshold specific material properties.

features.name: normalized_difference_green_red
features.description: Normalized difference between the green (550.90 nm) and red (650.80 nm) bands, scaling the difference by their sum.
features.expected_model_benefit: Offers an illumination-invariant index that tree models can use to split on relative spectral shape regardless of absolute intensity.
